finding.question: Did Nancy Pelosi say, in reference to US employers cutting workers’ hours, “Employers cutting hours is a good thing. It then gives that person time to pursue their dreams and passions,” and what was the context of her remarks?
finding.summary: The exact quotation appeared in a December 2013 blog post, but the post did not identify a recording or transcript of Pelosi saying it. In a September 2013 press conference, Pelosi did use similar language about following a passion rather than a health insurance policy: she argued that the Affordable Care Act would let people change jobs or start businesses without losing coverage. Fortune also reported in 2010 that Pelosi said the law would let people leave jobs they kept for insurance. Those documented remarks concerned workers’ choices, not employers cutting their hours.

sources.title: Transcript of Pelosi Press Conference Today
sources.snippet: That's transformational. [It's] about life, a healthier life, liberty, freedom, the liberty to pursue your happiness, whether you want to be a photographer, a writer, start your business, be self-employed, [and] change jobs. You're not job locked. You can follow your passion, not your policy, be job locked by your policy. It's entrepreneurial.

sources.title: Nancy Pelosi: Health care reform equals entrepreneurship
sources.snippet: “The entrepreneurial spirit of America is unleashed,” she said, because the bill allows people to leave unsatisfying jobs they keep only for the medical insurance. “I can take risks, I can be entrepreneurial, I can follow my passion,” she told the small audience gathered at the Paley Center for Media in New York. “I can change jobs without fearing that I’m hurting my family.”

report_raw.claim: House Speaker Nancy Pelosi said of US employers, “Employers cutting hours is a good thing. It then gives that person time to pursue their dreams and passions.”
report_raw.justification: A December 2013 blog post attributed the quoted words to Pelosi but did not identify a recording or transcript supporting the attribution [S3]. A September 2013 transcript shows Pelosi using similar language about following a passion, but she was discussing the freedom to change jobs or pursue other work without being locked into a job by health insurance [S1]. Fortune reported similar remarks in 2010 about leaving jobs kept for insurance, not employers cutting hours [S2]. Inference: Those documented remarks do not establish that Pelosi made the separate statement about employers cutting hours.
key_points: The exact quotation appears in a blog post that gives no primary source for it [S3].
Documented similar remarks concerned workers’ freedom to change jobs or pursue other work, not employers cutting hours [S1][S2].
No recording or contemporaneous transcript was found for the exact quotation.
report_raw.counter_argument: The blog’s attribution could support the claim, and Pelosi did use similar language about pursuing a passion [S3][S1]. But the blog provides no recording or transcript, and the documented remarks do not establish that she made the statement about employers cutting hours [S3][S1][S2].
evidence_gaps: A recording, contemporaneous transcript, or reliable independent report of the alleged remarks would help establish whether Pelosi said the exact words and in what context.
The origin of the quotation in the blog post remains unidentified.
